### Indianapolis (Marion County)

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-08-19 (Metropolitan Development Commission final unanimous 6-0 approval); the full City-County Council had voted 23-1 to advance the measure on 2026-08-10
- **Normalized date:** `2026-08-19` (exact)
- **Duration:** Effective through no later than Dec. 31, 2027
- **Current end date:** `2027-12-31`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `in-indianapolis-marion-county-undated`
- **Legal basis:** Proposal 238-2026, a zoning text amendment and moratorium, advanced by the City-County Council 23-1 on 2026-08-10 (sponsored by Council President Maggie Lewis, supported by Mayor Joe Hogsett) and given final unanimous (6-0) approval by the Metropolitan Development Commission on 2026-08-19
- **What prompted it:** Concern over the pace of recent data center approvals; council sought a pause while permanent zoning rules are finalized
- **Affected projects:** Would not affect previously approved projects (Metrobloks, Sabey) or applications already submitted (DC BLOX)
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23. The City-County Council voted 23-1 on 2026-08-10 to advance the moratorium, and the Metropolitan Development Commission gave final unanimous (6-0) approval on 2026-08-19, effective immediately and running through no later than Dec. 31, 2027. The three previously approved projects (DC Blox on the east side, Metrobloks in Martindale-Brightwood, and Sabey Corp. in southwest Marion County) remain exempt. The administration is convening an advisory committee (consultant selection Sept. 2026; industry research Oct. 2026; committee recommendations and a revised zoning ordinance by Aug. 2027).
- **Outcome:** City-County Council advanced the moratorium 23-1 on 2026-08-10; Metropolitan Development Commission gave final unanimous approval 2026-08-19, making Marion County's moratorium effective immediately through no later than Dec. 31, 2027.

### Miami County

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** ⚪ Replaced
- **Date enacted:** 2026-05-04
- **Normalized date:** `2026-05-04` (exact)
- **Duration:** Indefinite; remains in force until the county amends its zoning ordinance to regulate data centers
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `in-miami-county-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Ordinance Imposing Temporary Moratorium On The Development of Data Centers, adopted and recorded by the Board of Commissioners
- **What prompted it:** Bar the acceptance, processing, or approval of applications and permits, including improvement location permits, for data centers and appurtenant facilities in every zoning district of unincorporated Miami County while permanent regulations are drafted
- **Affected projects:** —
- **Detailed status:** Replaced as of 2026-09-23. At its 2026-07-20 meeting, the Miami County Board of Commissioners unanimously (3-0) approved a permanent data center regulatory ordinance amending the county zoning ordinance, ending the temporary moratorium that had been in force since 2026-05-04. The permanent ordinance permits data centers by-right in I-1, I-2, B-2, and B-3 districts and by special exception in Agricultural districts, and sets standards including a 55 dB sound limit at the property line, closed-loop or air-only cooling, underground utilities, 6-foot security fencing, and mandatory fire-department training.
- **Outcome:** Board of Commissioners unanimously (3-0) adopted a permanent data center zoning ordinance on 2026-07-20, replacing the temporary moratorium in force since 2026-05-04.
